result:
Post revisions are in, and `pnpm typecheck` passes. I didn't run the app or any tests, so none of the behaviour has been exercised.

- **Storage:** `db/schema.ts` has a new `postRevisions` table (`post_revisions`). I generated the migration with `void db generate`; it's `db/migrations/20261020001800_massive_masque.sql`, plus the snapshot and journal entry.
- **Keeping versions:** `lib/revisions.ts` has `updatePostKeepingRevision`, which saves the post's current title, excerpt and body as a revision and applies the new content in one batch. It also has `findRevisionOrFail`, which returns 404 when the revision belongs to a different post.
- **Edit and delete:** In `pages/posts/[id].server.ts`, `update` now goes through that helper. `delete` removes the post's revisions in the same batch as the post.
- **Edit authorization:** `update` had no author check before, so any signed-in user could edit anyone's post. I added `authorizeAuthor`, so a non-author now gets 403 on edit too. You didn't ask for this, but it's needed for "a refused edit keeps nothing".
- **History page:** `pages/posts/[id]/revisions.server.ts` and `revisions.tsx` list revisions newest first as `{ id, title, createdAt }`. Guests are redirected to `/login` and non-authors get 403. The post page has a "History" link for the author.
- **Restore:** `routes/posts/[id]/revisions/[revisionId]/restore.ts` handles `POST`. It applies the same guest and author checks, restores the revision's content, keeps the pre-restore version as a new revision, and redirects to `/posts/:id`. It leaves the restored revision in place.

Every save keeps a revision, including one that changes nothing, which you said isn't checked.
